sources.entry: napalm - Cross-vendor API to manipulate network devices.

summary.one_liner: NAPALM is a Python library that provides a unified API for interacting with and managing configurations and retrieving data from devices of multiple network router vendors.
summary.what_it_does: NAPALM (Network Automation and Programmability Abstraction Layer with Multivendor support) implements a set of functions to interact with different router vendor devices through one common API. The README says it supports several methods to connect to devices, to manipulate configurations, and to retrieve data. A separate link lists the supported network operating systems, and the README asks users to understand the caveats for each. It can be installed with pip and driven from the napalm CLI, which can call functions such as get_facts against a host. The README also describes integrations with Ansible (via the napalm-ansible project), SaltStack (built in since release 2016.11), and StackStorm (via a separate integration pack).
use_cases: manage configurations across multivendor routers and switches
retrieve facts and operational data from network devices
automate network device changes with Python
integrate network device control into Ansible playbooks
use network automation within SaltStack or StackStorm
check device connectivity with a command-line get_facts call
how_to_run: napalm --vendor VENDOR --user USERNAME --password PASSWORD --optional_args OPTIONAL_ARGS HOSTNAME call get_facts
notable: Single unified API across multiple router and network OS vendors
Command-line tool to test device connectivity with get_facts
Integration packs for Ansible and StackStorm via separate repositories
caveats: Supported devices and features vary by operating system; the README says to understand the caveats for each
Requires Python 3.9+ for release 5.1.0 and later
Some devices need specific setup, such as enabling the XML agent on IOS-XR or NXAPI on NXOS
